package application

import (
	"context"

	"metaldocs/internal/platform/authn"
)

// A3.3 negative fixture (Rule 2, DECLARATION form): the presence result thrown
// away by a `var` declaration rather than by an assignment.
//
// `actorID, _ := f(ctx)` is an AssignStmt. `var actorID, _ = f(ctx)` is a
// ValueSpec. To the compiler they are two spellings of one binding; to a walker
// they are unrelated node types, and a matcher written against the first form
// reports nothing on the second. The resulting variable is identical — "" on a
// request with no authenticated principal — so a guard that covers only the
// assignment is a guard with a documented spelling that turns it off.
//
// Both canonical accessors appear, because the ban is on discarding PRESENCE and
// not on one function: the bool-returning sibling and the error-returning one
// fail open in exactly the same way when their second result is dropped.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func settleDeclared(ctx context.Context) string {
	var actorID, _ = authn.UserIDFromContext(ctx)
	return actorID
}

func voidDeclared(ctx context.Context) string {
	var actorID, _ = authn.RequireUserID(ctx)
	return actorID
}
